findings.statement: JAK-STAT pathway activity is raised in all five cohorts (none down); the largest t is in GSE193677 [type=pathway_activity; source=ANALYSIS:pathways; per_cohort.GSE193677.t=15.68]. This pathway is already drug-targeted (JAK inhibitors), so it validates the approach but is not a new target.

Inferred STAT3 TF activity is up in all five cohorts, with t in GSE206285 of [type=tf_activity; source=ANALYSIS:pathways; per_cohort.GSE206285.t=24.0]. It is the downstream node shared by IL-6/gp130, OSM and JAK signalling, but inferred activity is not specific to any one upstream cytokine.

TNFa pathway activity is among the strongest and most consistent signals, up in all five cohorts, with t in GSE92415 of [type=pathway_activity; source=ANALYSIS:pathways; per_cohort.GSE92415.t=16.28]. TNF is already targeted by approved anti-TNF biologics; NFkB (also up in five cohorts) runs in parallel.

RELA (NFkB) TF activity is up in five of five cohorts, with t in GSE206285 of [type=tf_activity; source=ANALYSIS:pathways; per_cohort.GSE206285.t=21.24]. It reflects convergent inflammatory transcription (with AP1, STAT3, ATF family) rather than a single druggable circuit.

In the Gubatan single-cell data CXCL8 is made mostly by neutrophils (neutrophil share of transcripts [gene=CXCL8; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.873]), whereas in Smillie (no neutrophils captured) macrophages dominate, so the cellular source depends on whether neutrophils are captured. Bulk CXCL8 is up in five cohorts (meta log2FC [gene=CXCL8; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=3.704]).

Leading neutrophil-to-endothelium circuit: CXCL8 from neutrophils to ACKR1 endothelial cells is stronger in inflamed than uninflamed mucosa (log2 change [type=cell_communication; source=ANALYSIS:communication; log2_change=1.991]); Neutrophil CXCR4, OSM and MX1 states send the same signal. ACKR1 is an atypical chemokine receptor that presents chemokines, so this is a plausible recruitment route, but co-expression is not proof of signalling.

CXCR2 ranks first in the convergence ranking (meta log2FC [gene=CXCR2; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=2.264], same direction in five cohorts) and has clinical-stage antagonists (reparixin phase 3, navarixin, ladarixin, SX-682 phase 2), none established in UC. The receiving cells are neutrophils themselves: CXCL8 from Neutrophil CXCR4 to Neutrophil is up (log2 change [type=cell_communication; source=ANALYSIS:communication; log2_change=2.755]), an autocrine/paracrine neutrophil loop.

CXCR2 transcripts are overwhelmingly neutrophil in Gubatan (neutrophil share [gene=CXCR2; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.965]), while in Smillie, which lacks neutrophils, the signal is tiny and scattered over T/NK cells and the second dataset does not replicate it. The bulk rise therefore likely reflects neutrophil infiltration, not a change in tissue cells; targeting it means targeting neutrophil recruitment.

IL1B is up in five cohorts and ranks in the top twenty of the convergence list. In single cells its strongest inflamed-mucosa pairs go from monocyte-derived macrophages to neutrophil states via IL1R2, e.g. to Neutrophil CXCR4 (log2 change [type=cell_communication; source=ANALYSIS:communication; log2_change=2.059]). IL1R2 is a decoy receptor, so this pairing may reflect IL-1 buffering rather than signalling; IL-1 blockade exists (canakinumab) but is untested in UC here.

The neutrophil OSM to fibroblast circuit via IL6ST is weak: the Neutrophil OSM to LP fibroblast pair has a lower score in inflamed than uninflamed mucosa (log2 change [type=cell_communication; source=ANALYSIS:communication; log2_change=-0.709]); only a Neutrophil PADI4 to LP fibroblast pair appears newly in inflamed tissue, from a very low base. OSM itself is only a biomarker-profile candidate (rank 71), has no drugs and no genetics, so the neutrophil-OSM-inflammatory fibroblast hypothesis is not supported as a leading circuit here.

TGFb pathway activity is up in five cohorts with a very large t in GSE206285 [type=pathway_activity; source=ANALYSIS:pathways; per_cohort.GSE206285.t=25.17]. EGFR, hypoxia, MAPK, PI3K and VEGF pathways are also up in all five cohorts, so such broad pathway activation is non-discriminating, and none of these has a UC drug.

p53 activity is lower in three of five cohorts (for example GSE16879 t [type=pathway_activity; source=ANALYSIS:pathways; per_cohort.GSE16879.t=-3.59]) and not in the other two, so it is the only inconsistent-direction pathway. WNT is up in four cohorts but not significant in GSE73661 (padj [type=pathway_activity; source=ANALYSIS:pathways; per_cohort.GSE73661.padj=0.0637]), and Androgen is mixed (up in one, down in two), so these should not be called robust.

S100A8 (rank 19), like CHI3L1 and other secreted markers, is up in five cohorts in the convergence ranking but has no drug and no genetic evidence; these are better read as biomarkers of neutrophil/myeloid inflammation than as targets.

caveats: Pathway and TF activity are inferred from bulk biopsy transcripts (decoupler ulm); inflamed mucosa activates many pathways at once, so activity in five cohorts is not specificity.
Ligand-receptor scores are co-expression (ligand times receptor mean CP10K), not proof of signalling; ACKR1 and IL1R2 are atypical or decoy receptors.
Gubatan has neutrophils while Smillie has none, so cell-source shares differ between datasets; CXCR2 neutrophil dominance is not replicated in Smillie.
Case versus control cohorts mix inflamed and UC biopsies; no treatment-response data were used by this agent.
Drug stage information comes from Open Targets and does not imply UC efficacy; CXCR1/2 antagonists have no UC approval.
